page: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized server running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz with x86_64 architecture. The server features 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with dedicated CPU allocation and hyperthreading enabled. Hardware features include AVX and AES instruction sets. Cache configuration comprises 32 KB L1d cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 25 MB L3 cache per socket. Memory capacity stands at 122.0 GB, providing 7.62 GB of RAM per core.

Local storage is bundled directly with the instance as a 3200 GB NVMe SSD array, offering direct access to high-capacity local drives for input and output operations. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps. The instance contains no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core CPU capacity, PassMark database operation speeds, and Redis SET throughput. However, single-threaded operations and large block uncached write speeds show performance tradeoffs. Single-core Geekbench results, bzip3 decompression, and uncached memory write throughput fall into lower benchmark tiers due to the legacy CPU generation.

From a resource perspective, the high density of bundled local NVMe storage and memory relative to vCPUs provides cost efficiency for IO-bound applications. The instance is suited for high-throughput relational databases, NoSQL key-value stores, static web serving, and transactional data processing tasks where local disk bandwidth and capacity are prioritized over single-thread compute speed.
